# Generation 008B — information calibration

Generation 8B is Mode B. It calibrates the information statistics of the Generation 8A trajectories. It does not replace the context-repair atlas, and it does not run a new stochastic census. Pass and fail in this note are reserved for tests, replay, chronology, and numerical tolerances.

The numerical record is `constraint-lab/reports/generation-008b-round-b0-tables.json`. Schema `rs-constraint-lab.information-calibration-tables/v1`. File sha256 `d7bc06d027eabb62f5f2e5bed312c746ef3f062198a25a35bd5246ce23590e09`. Payload sha256 `b2ecdac74e38b3d53160a43b3319bcb4cc607cab4817c5cb2cfdaa68f4171adf`. The result commit is `dc9f9b9eb6e4a36b4513d10b49e937c43b57b371`. Every table row is labelled by layer: A is the plug-in, B is the permutation calibration, C is the deterministic kernel result. Float64 kernel quantities are deterministic kernel results. Mutual information is in nats. Negative values of plug-in minus null mean are stored as computed.

## A. External Review 008A

Review 008A is `constraint-lab/provenance/reviews/008A-chatgpt-review-v0.8a.md`. It reads branch `research/constraint-lab-v0.8a-context-repair` at `b7b5d848d90b7d1824bcce9740c2faf966cbea54`. The review inspected branch chronology, Round A0 frozen-plan ancestry, the rule-aware symmetry implementation, raw-context execution, trajectory and replay execution, the Round A0 report and synthesis, the mutual-information implementation, the current-context event counters, the CI history, and the final-head run.

The operational record it accepts is 6,144 primary trajectories, 6,759 durable items, 58 batches, 2 workers, 615 of 615 durable replay checks exact, 5,314,418 full events, 3,145,728 pair events, 3,145,728 transition markers, 0 timeouts, 0 retries, 0 quarantines, and every episode at `pair_horizon`. Disk after merge is 678,150,248 bytes. Batch wall times are median 17.716 s, p90 18.063 s, maximum 19.428 s. The A0 frozen plan is `61ed53075238284850e792aff5743f0a8a7b6695`. The atlas result is `4897d9e02b2942670bafc52bc966ef6709167b64`, and it descends from that plan. Final-head Actions run `38312376920` is on `b7b5d848d90b7d1824bcce9740c2faf966cbea54`. The earlier red runs were a shallow checkout. Commit `bf821c771e4ed86e24688ed44ab6035b7e9af785` set full history on the constraint-lab job. The suite after that fix reported 167 passed.

Prompt 008A authored metadata, recorded beside the agent input and not assigned to it: 33,117 bytes, sha256 `0417394f876ad063a48759ef419102b4fde4730f710e228ebba9703209c6b3f6`. The stored agent input is 33,115 bytes, sha256 `1c44d30b086e2e02ace4d0777605267d8f7139c71948beffe058b5c976d25010`. The authored file is not in this working environment. Status `externally_verified_pending_import`. Relationship `unknown`.

## B. Why plug-in mutual information required calibration

Generation 8A computed ordinary plug-in mutual information and conditional mutual information from finite contingency tables. That estimator is the standard functional of the empirical table. The Generation 8A implementation has no finite-sample bias correction, no permutation reference, and no replacement by the transition kernel.

The laboratory has a 1024-state chain and an explicit transition law, so those three layers can be separated. Layer A is the Generation 8A plug-in. Layer B compares it with a deterministic permutation null. Layer C evaluates the same estimand from the kernel. A non-zero plug-in value is a statement about the estimator until a zero-information control or a kernel quantity says otherwise.

The leading independence-bias scale for 16 contexts, 2 destinations, and 256 episodes is `((16-1)*(2-1))/(2*256) = 0.029297` nats. That figure is a sanity check. The primary correction is the permutation null and the kernel value.

## C. Structural zero-information controls

R00, R03, and R07 are calibration instruments supplied by the rule semantics. They are references for the estimator. The programme is not organised as a hypothesis test.

`Constraint.matches` reads the action bit, each condition bit, and, when a count literal is present, the popcount of the full state. The A0 palette has no count literals. R00 has no rules, so every slot weight is 1. R03 is `dissolve(0-1) => strong_suppress`. R07 is `dissolve(0-1) => strong_favour`. In both, the only modified weight is pair slot 0, and it is modified only when pair bit 0 is set. No action, condition, or count reads a triad slot. For a fixed pair mask the six pair-slot weights are therefore the same at all 16 triads. The measured triad weight span on these three systems is 0.

Between pair events only triad bits toggle. On these three systems that excursion leaves the weight vector unchanged. The pair slot that ends the excursion, and the pair mask it writes, are independent of the current triad once the current pair mask is known. By induction the whole pair-mask trajectory is independent of the initial triad. Every functional of that trajectory is independent of the initial triad: the first other 3-edge destination, the graph class at a checkpoint, the edge count, the class given the edge count, the labelled pair mask, and the expected class occupancy. Under a uniform raw-triad prior the exact mutual information of each of those observables with the initial triad is zero.

The same weight identity gives the current-context statement. The local law `P(next pair slot | full pair mask, current triad)` equals `P(next pair slot | full pair mask)`. Conditional mutual information of the triad with the next pair slot, given the full pair mask, is zero under the balanced weighting, under the A0 empirical state weighting with the exact slot law, and under the stationary pair-event weighting. Conditioning only on the isomorphism class is a different estimand. Different masks in one class can carry different slot laws, and a finite sample can put different mask weights on different triads inside that class.

The runtime classification matches this reading. R00, R03, and R07 are the structural zero controls. R01, R02, R04, R05, and R06 each name triad slot 6 in a condition. Their triad weight spans are 0.75, except R06, whose strong-favour grade has span 3.0.

## D. Frozen B0 analysis plan

The frozen analysis plan is commit `466d54339738d315ed621ea4256a239cb026498a`, plan hash `279857bb2ee82eefd430ba56c9fa3758238ebea9e0b652c01b56b97dbc1bf618`, file `constraint-lab/exploration/generation-008b/round-b0-plan.json`. It was pushed before any B0 quantity was computed. Actions run `38319517214` succeeded on that commit. The result commit descends from it. Journey step 1 still has `result_commit` null. Journey step 2 names `dc9f9b9eb6e4a36b4513d10b49e937c43b57b371`.

B0 is the only round. The palette is the Generation 8A repair palette, R00 through R07. No new scientific episodes. Permutation counts were frozen at 10,000 for each initial-context cell and 2,000 for each current-context cell. Seeds are `sha256-u64-v1` of the experiment id, the estimand id, the system, the source graph, and the permutation index. The zero-information floor is `1e-10`. Kernel row tolerance `1e-9`. Stationary and hitting residuals `1e-8`. Cross-solver tolerance `1e-8`. Plug-in reproduction tolerance `1e-9`. Chain-rule tolerance `1e-9`. Unabsorbed-mass tolerance `1e-8`.

Each command is one system, or one system and source. Two workers. Watchdog 120 seconds. The commands that ran were `exact`, `permute-initial`, and `permute-current`. Exact kernels are built once per system and reused. A horizon-matched destination mutual information is omitted when the unabsorbed mass at epoch 512 is below `1e-8`. The validation table stores that mass. The largest mass in B0 is `2.460e-22`, on R05. The episode-block bootstrap was left unused.

The first `exact` command for R03 stopped because an empirical class-conditional value on a zero-information control was above the floor. That value is an occupancy correlation inside a graph class. Commit `7eb6392` keeps the floor on the full-mask identity, which is the identity the semantics give. R03 was rerun. The frozen estimands did not change. The published tables include that rerun.

## E. Plug-in reproduction

The committed Generation 8A cells were recomputed from the committed counts with the same mutual-information functions. The comparison covers 336 cells: 24 first-destination cells, 240 checkpoint class cells, and 72 current-context cells. The maximum absolute gap is `2.810e-16`, inside the tolerance `1e-9`. Contingency order does not enter the functional. The unit remains nats.

The Generation 8A plug-in figures below are therefore the same numbers as the published A0 tables. Calibration starts from that reproduction.

## F. Permutation calibration

Initial-context permutations shuffle the 16 raw-triad labels inside each system and source. Episode outcomes stay put. Each label keeps 16 episodes. Current-context permutations shuffle the triad inside each conditioner stratum and preserve the outcome and conditioner marginals. Pair events inside an episode are serially correlated. The current-context null is a finite-table bias calibration. Its percentile is not a trajectory uncertainty and it is not a causal significance statement. No p-value is published. Plug-in minus null mean is stored with its sign.

### First destination

The permutation-null mean on all 24 cells lies between 0.03024 and 0.03127 nats. The Miller-Madow full-alphabet term is 0.029297 nats on every cell. The plug-in values sit on that bias scale.

| System | Source | Plug-in | Null mean | Excess | Null percentile | Exact |

| R00 | path | 0.03071 | 0.03052 | +0.00019 | 55.8 | floor |
| R00 | triangle | 0.04342 | 0.03093 | +0.01249 | 86.8 | floor |

| R06 | star | 0.02750 | 0.03062 | −0.00312 | 43.5 | 1.906e-7 |

"Floor" means the absolute exact-kernel value is below `1e-10`. The signed kernel values on those cells have magnitude at most about `2e-16`. R03 star is the largest plug-in cell, 0.07021 nats. Its null 95th percentile is 0.0525 and its null 99th is 0.0642. The cell is in the far tail of its own null, and its exact-kernel value is at the floor. R07 triangle is the low tail of the same family of controls: plug-in 0.01273, excess −0.01841, percentile 2.7, exact value at the floor. The controls track the bias, including both tails.

### Checkpoints

From checkpoint 2 through 512 the median plug-in class mutual information of the 24 system/source cells lies between 0.1209 and 0.1398 nats. The median permutation-null mean on those same cells lies between 0.1315 and 0.1328 nats. The full-alphabet Miller-Madow term is 0.29297 nats, which counts 11 classes. The realised support is smaller, and the permutation null is the calibration that matches the plug-in. Excess at checkpoint 512 runs in both directions. R00 path is 0.1243 against a null mean of 0.1320. R01 star is 0.1798 against 0.1332. Both exact-kernel values at that checkpoint are at the floor.

At checkpoint 1 the null mean is about 0.030 on star and triangle and about 0.097 on path, because one pair toggle from a 3-edge source reaches a smaller set of classes, and the path source reaches more than one class at the neighbouring edge counts.

### Current context

For `I(current triad; next pair slot | full pair mask)` the permutation-null mean is 0.01850 to 0.01868 nats on every system and source. The plug-in on R00, R03, and R07 is 0.01782 to 0.01919. Excess on those controls is a few ten-thousandths of a nat, positive and negative. R07 star is percentile 1.7. R00 star is percentile 96.5. The plug-in on the five triad-conditioned systems is 0.02939 to 0.03624. Every one of those 15 cells sits at the top of its 2,000-draw null. The largest plug-in is R06 star, 0.03624, against a null mean of 0.01855.

The class-conditional plug-in nulls are smaller, because the conditioner is coarser: about 0.00316 nats for the next slot, and about 0.00097 nats for the next class. Those floors are the right comparison for the Generation 8A class-conditional plug-in figures.

## G. Exact first-destination information

The route definition is unchanged. The source 3-edge class is transient. The other two 3-edge classes compete. Return to the source is allowed. The quantity is the eventual hitting distribution. The two destination probabilities sum to 1. The largest gap in that sum, on R00, is `3.33e-15`. Unabsorbed mass at epoch 512 is at most `2.460e-22`.

Under the uniform raw-triad prior the exact-kernel mutual information is at the floor for R00, R03, and R07 on every source. It is at the floor on the path source for every system, including the triad-conditioned ones. On star and triangle it is non-zero for the triad-conditioned systems, and the star value agrees with the triangle value to about `1e-16`.

The largest exact value is R05, `2.025e-5` nats, on star and on triangle. R01 is `5.699e-7`. R02 and R04 are `3.307e-7`. R06 is `1.906e-7`. Each of these is above the floor `1e-10` and small relative to the plug-in, which is about 0.02 to 0.07, and small relative to the permutation-null mean, which is about 0.031.

The Generation 8A maximum, R03 star at 0.0702 nats, is one of the cells whose exact value is at the floor. R05 triangle, plug-in 0.0567 and null percentile 97.2, has exact value `2.025e-5`. The plug-in excess there is 0.0255. The kernel value is three orders of magnitude smaller.

Sampling frequencies from the A0 episodes sit at the scale expected from 16 replicates. Pooled L1 distances from the exact destination law run up to about 0.125. That comparison is a compatibility check at the sampling scale. The information result is the kernel value.

## H. Exact checkpoint information

The pair-class distribution at checkpoints 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 is the epoch-0 start propagated by the pair-event kernel. Sampled trajectories are not the source of these distributions.

On R00, R03, and R07 the exact class mutual information, the edge-count mutual information, the class-given-edge mutual information, and the labelled pair-mask mutual information are at the floor at every sampled checkpoint. Magnitudes are at most a few `1e-16`, and the stored signs include both.

On the triad-conditioned systems the exact class information is largest at checkpoint 1 or 2 and is at the floor from checkpoint 64 through 512. Nothing in the exact class curve persists to checkpoint 512. The plug-in median near 0.12 nats through checkpoint 512 sits on the permutation-null median near 0.132. Persistence of the plug-in number is the bias of the estimator.

The largest exact class value in the grid is R06 path at checkpoint 1, 0.02798 nats. R06 star and triangle at checkpoint 1 are 0.008801 nats. R01 path at checkpoint 1 is 0.01023 nats. R01 star and triangle peak at checkpoint 2, at 0.002113 nats. R02 and R04 peak at 0.0001206 nats on star and triangle at checkpoint 2, and their curves agree with each other to `1.2e-16`. R05 peaks at 0.0001640 nats on star and triangle at checkpoint 4. By checkpoint 32 the largest exact class value among the conditioned systems is `1.29e-9`, on R01. By checkpoint 64 every exact class value is at the floor.

Star and triangle agree with each other to about `1e-16` at every system and checkpoint. The labelled pair-mask mutual information agrees across all three sources to about `1e-16`. It is larger than the class information at the early checkpoints: 0.02798 on R06 and 0.01023 on R01 at checkpoint 1, and 0.02986 on R06 at checkpoint 2. It is at the floor by checkpoint 64 as well.

## I. Edge-count versus shape decomposition

Edge count is a function of graph class, so the chain rule `I(T0; C) = I(T0; E) + I(T0; C | E)` is an identity of the joint distribution. The numerical gap is at most `5.94e-16`.

At checkpoint 1 on star and triangle, the exact class information equals the exact edge-count information, and the shape term is 0. One pair toggle changes the edge count by exactly one, and from those sources that determines the class. At checkpoint 1 on path the shape term is present. For R06 path it is 0.01918 of the 0.02798 class nats, and the edge term is 0.008801. For R01 path it is 0.008838 of the 0.01023 class nats, and the edge term is 0.001393. The edge term itself agrees between path and star to about `1e-16`. The extra path information is shape given edge count.

At checkpoint 2 the shape term is a real piece of the remaining class information. On star and triangle it is the larger piece for R02, R04, and R05: R02 and R04 have edge 0.0000177 and shape 0.000103; R05 has edge 0.0000287 and shape 0.000131. R01 and R06 at checkpoint 2 are still mostly edge count, with a shape piece of 0.000121 on R01 and 0.000269 on R06.

The labelled mask decomposes the same way: mask information equals class information plus mask-given-class. At the early checkpoints the mask term is the larger one. The additional information is the labelled alignment inside a class. By checkpoint 64 the mask term is at the floor with the class term.

The deferred Generation 8A question, whether a persistent 0.12 nats is edge count or residual shape, has this answer in the kernel. There is no persistent 0.12 nats. The early exact information is both coordinates, in proportions that depend on the checkpoint and the source, and both coordinates have decayed below the floor by checkpoint 64.

## J. Exact finite-horizon occupancy

Expected occupancy is the mean of the class distribution over pair epochs 1 through 512 inclusive. Epoch 0, the initial source, is excluded. Generation 8A occupancy included the initial epoch. The context range is the maximum minus the minimum across the 16 raw triads.

On R00, R03, and R07 the exact dense-minus-sparse range is at most `5.6e-16`, and the 11-class L1 range is at most `1.8e-15`. The exact context range on the controls is at the floor.

On the triad-conditioned systems the dense-minus-sparse range is non-zero and small beside the Generation 8A raw spans of about 0.06 to 0.09:

| System | Dense minus sparse | Sparse share | 3-edge share | Dense share | Class L1, star and triangle | Class L1, path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R01 | 0.001423 | 0.000720 | 0.000017 | 0.000703 | 0.001476 | 0.001626 |
| R02 | 0.000395 | 0.000205 | 0.000015 | 0.000190 | 0.000441 | 0.000410 |
| R04 | 0.000395 | 0.000190 | 0.000015 | 0.000205 | 0.000441 | 0.000410 |
| R05 | 0.000347 | 0.000146 | 0.000054 | 0.000201 | 0.000546 | 0.000487 |
| R06 | 0.001925 | 0.000974 | 0.000024 | 0.000950 | 0.002000 | 0.002345 |

R06 is the largest. The per-triad dense-minus-sparse values agree across star, path, and triangle to about `1e-15`. The scalar edge-count range is source-invariant at that precision. The 11-class L1 range is larger on path for R01 and R06, and larger on star and triangle for R02, R04, and R05. R02 and R04 exchange the sparse-share range and the dense-share range and otherwise agree. Their per-triad dense-minus-sparse vectors are not negations of each other.

Checkpoint 512 itself carries no exact initial-triad information. The occupancy range is the average of a transient difference over 512 epochs. It is a finite-horizon integral. It is a genuine context dependence of the path average, and it is about 0.002 at its largest.

## K. Current-context exact transition-law information

The estimand is the one Generation 8A counted: the triad in the pre-pair-event state, and the pair slot of the next pair event. Triad-event slots are outside the outcome. At each full state the exact conditional slot law is the six pair propensities renormalised among themselves. That is the local law of the pair-event records. For a triad-conditioned rule it differs from the epoch-kernel next-slot law, because triad flips during the excursion can change the weights before the pair event.

Three weightings stay separate.

Balanced-law weighting gives every pair-mask and triad state equal weight before the exact slot law is applied. It is one number per system. It asks whether the rule itself makes the next slot depend on the triad once the mask is fixed.

A0 empirical-source weighting uses the visited pre-pair-event states in the Generation 8A streams, 131,072 pair events per system and source, and replaces the sampled slot with the exact slot distribution at that state. It asks what the finite atlas experienced, with the next-event sampling noise removed.

Stationary pair-event weighting uses the stationary distribution of the full-event chain. The joint weight of a state and a pair slot is stationary mass times the full-event probability of that pair slot. It asks what the long-run pair-event clock experiences.

Full pair mask, next pair slot, exact-kernel conditional mutual information:

| System | Balanced | A0 empirical, three sources | Stationary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R00 | floor | floor | floor |
| R01 | 0.009749 | 0.012064 to 0.012180 | 0.012025 |
| R02 | 0.009749 | 0.011894 to 0.011974 | 0.012025 |
| R03 | floor | floor | floor |
| R04 | 0.009749 | 0.011882 to 0.011950 | 0.012025 |
| R05 | 0.010413 | 0.012953 to 0.013164 | 0.013240 |
| R06 | 0.023368 | 0.016842 to 0.017076 | 0.016895 |
| R07 | floor | floor | floor |

R00, R03, and R07 are at the floor on all three weightings. The signed balanced values have magnitude about `1e-15`. The identity holds. R01, R02, and R04 agree with one another through about `1e-15` on the balanced value and on the stationary value.

R06 is the largest balanced value, 0.02337 nats, and its stationary and empirical values are smaller, about 0.0169. The long-run occupancy experiences less of that rule's intrinsic dependence than the balanced weighting measures. R01, R02, R04, and R05 go the other way by a smaller amount: the stationary value is a little above the balanced value, and the A0 empirical exact-law value sits on the stationary value.

The plug-in excess over the permutation null tracks these exact-law values. R06 star has plug-in 0.03624, null mean 0.01855, excess 0.01769, and exact empirical-source value 0.01691. The Generation 8A interval of about 0.030 to 0.036 nats is the exact-law value plus a bias of about 0.0185 nats. Subtracting 0.018 by hand is not the calculation. The kernel value is.

## L. Balanced versus empirical versus stationary weighting

The three numbers answer three questions.

The balanced value is law dependence. Once the labelled pair mask is fixed, the next pair-slot distribution depends on the current triad exactly on the five systems whose rule names a triad, and it is independent of the triad on R00, R03, and R07.

The stationary value is the same law, weighted by the pair events the chain produces in the long run. For the strong-suppress conditionals it is about 0.012 to 0.013 nats. For the strong-favour conditional it is 0.0169 nats, below that rule's balanced value of 0.0234.

The A0 empirical-source value is the finite 512-epoch atlas with the exact slot law. On every triad-conditioned system it agrees with the stationary value to about 0.001 nats or closer. The exploratory trajectories already sat on the long-run state weighting for this local estimand. The gap between the plug-in and this value is the finite-table bias, whose null mean is about 0.0185 nats.

## M. Full pair mask versus graph class

The full-mask quantity stays primary. The class-conditional exact-law quantities are the continuity comparison with Generation 8A.

Stationary pair-event weighting, exact-kernel conditional mutual information:

| System | Slot given full mask | Slot given class | Fraction retained | Next class given class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R00 | floor | floor |  | floor |
| R01 | 0.012025 | 0.007946 | 0.661 | 0.000972 |
| R02 | 0.012025 | 0.007946 | 0.661 | 0.000972 |
| R03 | floor | floor |  | floor |
| R04 | 0.012025 | 0.007946 | 0.661 | 0.000972 |
| R05 | 0.013240 | 0.009400 | 0.710 | 0.002571 |
| R06 | 0.016895 | 0.007492 | 0.443 | 0.001196 |
| R07 | floor | floor |  | floor |

Collapsing the labelled mask to the 11-class label keeps about two thirds of the stationary slot information for R01, R02, R04, and R05, and keeps 0.443 of it for R06. The discarded fraction is labelled alignment. The next graph class, given the current class, carries still less: at most 0.00257 nats, on R05.

On the zero-information controls the stationary class-conditional values are at the floor. The pair-mask chain does not depend on the triad, so the long-run mix of masks inside a class does not either. The A0 empirical-source class-conditional values are different. R00 remains at the floor, because every slot weight is 1. R03 and R07 are about `1e-5` to `5e-5`: R03 star next-class-given-class is `1.372e-5`, and R07 path next-slot-given-class is `4.921e-5`. The slot law of an unconditional dissolve depends on whether pair bit 0 is set. A finite atlas can correlate the triad with which masks inside a class were visited. That residual is an occupancy correlation in the sample. It is above the floor, it is far below the 0.018 plug-in, and it is not a failure of the full-mask identity.

The Generation 8A plug-in comparison, about 0.003 nats given the class and about 0.018 nats given the mask on the controls, compares two bias floors. The exact law on the controls is at the floor for the full mask under every weighting, and at the floor for the class under the stationary weighting. On the triad-conditioned systems the exact class-conditional slot information is about 0.0075 to 0.0094 nats. The plug-in of about 0.010 to 0.013 sits above its own null mean of about 0.00316 by that same amount.

## N. Numerical validation

The published validation rows, one per system:

Kernel row error is between `1.1e-16` and `4.4e-16`. Stationary residual is between `1.5e-16` and `1.1e-15`, inside the `1e-8` threshold of the float64 solver. Arithmetic is float64. Every system reports period 2, and the stationary distribution is still unique under that period when the chain is irreducible. Hitting residual is between `7.8e-16` and `1.7e-15`. Dense and block epoch kernels agree to between `1.4e-17` and `1.1e-16`. Rule-aware symmetry gaps on the destination laws are at most `1.6e-15`. Destination probabilities sum to 1 within `3.3e-15`. Chain-rule gaps are at most `5.9e-16`. Unabsorbed mass at epoch 512 is at most `2.460e-22`.

## D. The minimal local rule

The W4 alphabet is base 2. `strong_suppress` is grade −2, factor `1/4`. `strong_favour` is grade +2, factor `4`. The kernel gives every slot baseline weight 1 and multiplies a slot by the factor when a constraint matches that slot. The pair-event law renormalises the six pair weights.

A match requires the action slot to be the toggled slot, the action bit to be in the polarity's admissible state, and each condition bit to agree. For one conditional pair rule the admissible state is one bit, and the condition in this palette is one triad bit. Enumeration over all 1024 states puts the six-slot law into two values. It is uniform when the rule is inactive. It is the one-slot reweight when the action is admissible and the gate matches. The other eight bits do not split either group. The exact weight gap against the implementation is `0/1`. There are 256 active states.

The one-bit conjunction of admissibility and the gate is a sufficient statistic for this local law. The two raw bits are also sufficient, and three of their four pairs share the uniform law, so the conjunction is the smaller statistic. Neither statistic is claimed to determine the future trajectory. Later pair masks depend on which slot was chosen, and the gate continues to move.

R01 is `dissolve(0-1) | absent(0-1-2) => strong_suppress`. R02 is `form(0-1) | absent(0-1-2) => strong_suppress`. R04 is `dissolve(2-3) | present(0-1-2) => strong_suppress`. R06 is `dissolve(0-1) | absent(0-1-2) => strong_favour`. Each names one action slot and one gate.

## E. Closed-form pair-slot law

When the rule is inactive, each of the six pair slots has probability `1/6`. When the rule is active and exactly one slot carries multiplier `m`,

```text
q(action) = m / (m + 5)
q(other)  = 1 / (m + 5)
```

For `m = 1/4` the action probability is `1/21` and each other probability is `4/21`. For `m = 4` the action probability is `4/9` and each other probability is `1/9`. Every relevant state in the 1024-state enumeration matches these rows.

Under the balanced weighting, 32 of 64 pair masks make the action admissible, and on each of those masks 8 of 16 triads match the gate. The remaining masks contribute zero. The balanced conditional mutual information is therefore

```text
I_balanced = (1/2) JS(q_0, q_m)
```

with equal weight on the two gate states inside an admissible mask. This factor is the state count.

## R. Local edge-count drift

For a pair event, formation changes the edge count by `+1` and dissolution by `−1`. The expected change is the six-slot law contracted with those signs. The baseline, with uniform slots, depends only on how many edges are present. The rule-induced part is the difference between the gated law and that baseline.

On an active rule the induced part has a closed form in the edge count `k`. Strong-suppress dissolution contributes `(6−k)/21`. Strong-favour dissolution contributes `(k−6)/9`. Strong-suppress formation contributes `−k/21`. The gate must match and the action must be admissible. Every other stratum contributes 0, including a dissolution rule on the complete graph, where every slot already removes an edge, and a formation rule on the empty graph. ## V. Inferences

Path topology converts a one-slot bias into shape-given-edge information, because the biased slot is the middle edge and that edge has a private class inside its edge count. Star and triangle convert the same kind of bias into edge count only, because every toggle at a given edge count shares a class.

Initial-context information decays because the gate bit is refreshed by triad toggles. The other triad bits are not what the pair mask remembers. After the initial bit is forgotten, the current bit still gates the transition. The two statements are readings of one rule at two times.

The Generation 8 occupancy axis has the sign of the local edge drift. Unconditional rules produce a larger balanced drift than one-gate rules of the same grade, and their occupancy shifts are larger in that direction. The stationary distribution is not given by the drift mean.

R01, R02, and R04 are the same balanced local mechanism. Their source trajectories differ where the named action is inadmissible. R05's extra local information is a shared denominator, which is a different fact from its multistep composition residual.

## W. RS / global-coherence interpretation

Inside this model, a higher-order bit can be locally effective and globally forgotten as an initial condition. The effect that persists is the bias of the rule that reads whatever bit is present, and that bias is visible as an occupancy shift that unconditional pair rules can also produce, often more strongly. Local higher-order dependence is therefore a real feature of the transition law and a weak diagnostic of a higher-order ontology. The large occupancy axis is robust and, on this palette, mostly a grade effect.

Nothing here shows that a physical or biological system uses this grammar. Nothing here infers a designer. The H=0 forgetting is a property of a state that stores the current relations and not a history. It is an observation about that state. A small exact gate can still be the mechanism of a larger coordinate, as the drift sign shows, without the gate's information being large and without its initial value lasting.

The coherence ledger keeps those dimensions apart. The local information is small, exact, and local. The occupancy shift is large, robust, and stationary, and its higher-order specificity is limited by the unconditional rules. The initial-context footprint is very small and transient.

# Generation 008D errata

This file corrects the scope of several sentences in the Generation 8D report. It does not replace that report. The historical report, its tables and the historical coherence statements stay in place. No 8D number changes, and no recomputation is required.

## 1. The no-gate-product result is a property of the K=2 subgrammar

Generation 8D showed, correctly, that two primitive one-condition rules on one action cannot create an independent gate×gate coefficient in logit space. For two distinct gate literals:

```text
L(G1, G2) = c + λ1 l1(G1) + λ2 l2(G2)
L11 − L10 − L01 + L00 = 0
```

This holds on all 272 same-action two-gate systems of the D0 census.

Several sentences of the report broaden that result beyond what it establishes:

- the inference in §V that XOR of two gates, and any independent tuning of the both-active state, "need a grammar in which one constraint can modulate another";
- the interpretation in §W that two higher-order constraints "cannot express a relation between the two conditions themselves";
- candidate G in §X, which calls meta-constraints, `L > 0`, "the smallest grammar in which one constraint modulates another, and so the first place a gate-by-gate logit coefficient or a two-gate XOR could appear";
- the closing sentence of §Y, which describes an edge "from the gate-product bound to the meta-constraint question".

**Correction.** The zero gate×gate logit coefficient is a property of the Generation 8D subgrammar: two primitive K=2 rules, each with one triad literal. It is not a bound on the full ordinary constraint language. In the order-3 independent hypergraph, `Constraint.k() = 1 + len(conditions) + len(counts)`, and the parser accepts several conditions joined by `&`. A K=3 rule with two conjunctive triad literals, such as `dissolve(0-1) | present(0-1-2) & present(0-1-3) => strong_favour`, is already executable in the existing DSL. It may introduce a genuine second-order gate interaction without `L > 0`. Generation 8E examines it.

## 2. The opening compression overstates "genuinely two-gate"

The report's opening paragraph ends: "Everything else is genuinely two-gate at the local law."

**Correction.** Beyond the exact eliminations, the syntax partitions into zero-, one- and two-effective-gate laws. The census gives 16 weighted canonical systems at effective gate dimension 0, 960 at dimension 1 and 2,608 at dimension 2. So 2,608 of the 3,584 weighted canonical systems need two distinct triad bits locally. The 960 dimension-one systems, the R1T and R2S classes, are not two-gate at the local law. Of the 2,608 dimension-two systems, 256 never activate both rules in one state.

The compression this round supports is short. Each primitive rule is one feature: the conjunction of its action's admissibility literal and its gate literal, carrying one log weight. Two rules add their features in the log weight of the slot they name. Six-slot normalisation turns that sum into a probability law, and it couples slots only through the shared denominator. On one action slot the log multiplier is an affine function of the gate literals, with no gate-by-gate coefficient. Exact collapses occur where the affine function loses a variable: complementary gates with equal weights, and opposite directions on one gate with equal weights. Exact syntactic twins occur where two different literal choices give the same affine function. Everything else is genuinely two-gate at the local law, and the balanced information does not see placement, direction, or literal polarity at all.

## G. Local softmax grammar

For a two-rule system the pair-event law is

```text
q(e | x) ∝ exp( λ1 φ1(x, e) + λ2 φ2(x, e) ),    λi = ln mi
```

where `φi(x, e) = 1` exactly when rule `i` names slot `e`, its action is admissible at `x` (the edge is absent for a formation, present for a dissolution), and its gate literal is true at `x`. Each primitive feature is therefore a two-literal conjunction: one admissibility literal on the slot's own bit, one gate literal on a triad bit.

The implementation agrees with this form on every system. For all 3584 weighted systems, the implementation kernel weights equal the product formula on all 1024 states as exact fractions, gap 0. The log-weight residual `log w(x, e) − (λ1 φ1 + λ2 φ2)` has maximum absolute value `2.22e-16` over every state and pair slot of every system, the float64 rounding of `ln` on exact fractions. The primitive two-rule composition is exactly additive in log weight.

That is feature composition. It is a statement about the DSL's algebra. It does not say that probabilities, informations, drifts, or trajectory observables add.

## K. Same-action different-gate composition

Two rules on the same action and two different triads give the action four levels,

```text

0  0    1
1  0    m1
0  1    m2
1  1    m1*m2
```

where `Gi` is literal truth, not the raw triad bit. On all 272 systems in the family the both-active row was checked against `m1*m2/(m1*m2+5)` on the action and `1/(m1*m2+5)` elsewhere, gap 0, and the logit interaction

```text

```

is 0 on every system. Two primitive one-gate rules do not create a gate-by-gate logit coefficient.

The levels coincide in two ways. When `m1 = m2`, the two single-active rows are the same law. When `m1*m2 = 1`, the both-active row returns to the uniform law. Each gives three distinct rows: 80 systems with equal weights, 64 with reciprocal weights. The remaining 128 systems have four rows.

Reciprocal weights also produce syntactic twins. On one slot the log multiplier is

```text
L = c + β1 G1 + β2 G2        (Gi now the raw triad bits)
```

A present literal with log weight `λ` contributes `β = λ`. An absent literal contributes `β = −λ` and adds `λ` to `c`. Flipping both literals and inverting both weights keeps `(β1, β2)` and changes `c` by `−(λ1 + λ2)`, so the law is unchanged exactly when `m1*m2 = 1`. For example

```text
dissolve(0-1) | absent(0-1-2)  => strong_favour
dissolve(0-1) | absent(0-2-3)  => strong_suppress
```

and

```text
dissolve(0-1) | present(0-1-2) => strong_suppress
dissolve(0-1) | present(0-2-3) => strong_favour
```

have the identical labelled weight table: both are `L = ln 4 · (G_023 − G_012)`. Sixteen labelled-law coincidences across orbits are of this kind. Eight more coincide only after a vertex permutation. Together with the eight complementary coincidences in section J, these are all of the cross-orbit coincidences in the census: 24 labelled, 32 under S4. The local law determines `(c, β1, β2)`. It does not determine which literals were written.

## M. Different-action different-gate composition

Two actions on different slots read two different triads. Where both actions are admissible there are four activation combinations, and the logit vector is

```text
z = λ1 G1 e_a + λ2 G2 e_b
```

Each gate moves its own coordinate of the slot-logit vector. The logits add, coordinate by coordinate, with no cross term. The probabilities do not: when both are active, slot `a`'s probability is `m1/(m1+m2+4)`, which depends on `m2`. That dependence is the normalisation interaction. It is a property of the denominator, not of a gate-by-gate coefficient.

The opposite-direction family is the one place where two rules on one slot cannot coexist. Form is admissible only where the edge is absent and dissolve only where it is present, so the two rules are never active together.

On one triad with the same literal and equal weights the slot's own bit drops out (section H). The law is a gated toggle: slot `e` carries `m` whenever the literal is true, whatever the edge state. On one triad with opposite literals and equal weights, for example `ORB-0027-W00`,

## P. Truth-table expressivity

On one action with two distinct gate literals, the log multiplier over the four literal states is

```text
L(G1, G2) = c + λ1 l1(G1) + λ2 l2(G2)
```

with `li` the chosen literal of `Gi`. Every such table satisfies `Δ12 L = 0`, so `L11 = L10 + L01 − L00`. That gives the exact answers to the three questions.

There is no independently tunable conjunction term. The both-active level is fixed by the other three.

XOR between two gates cannot be isolated. An XOR table needs `L00 = L11 ≠ L10 = L01`, so `Δ12 L = −2(L10 − L00) ≠ 0`. A literal flip replaces `li` by `1 − li`, which changes `c` and the sign of `λi` and leaves `Δ12 L = 0`. No choice of literals or weights reaches XOR.

The both-active state cannot be moved while the other three are fixed. The nearest available shape is `L11 = L00`, reached only with `λ2 = −λ1`, which forces `L10 = −L01`. The reciprocal systems of section K realise that shape.

The bound is about two gate literals. Between a slot's own bit and one gate bit, XOR is realised by two rules, `ORB-0027-W00` in section M, because admissibility and the gate literal are already conjoined inside each primitive feature. The surface item records the bound as a statement. The evidence is the derivation above and the 272 measured `Δ12 L = 0` identities.

## V. Inferences

The current DSL composes constraints as additive features in event-logit space. Each primitive feature is the conjunction of an admissibility literal and one gate literal. A system's local law is the softmax of the sum of its active features. Within this grammar, that sentence is exact.

Two primitive one-gate rules cannot create a gate-by-gate logit coefficient. The most two gates can do on one slot is an affine function of two literals. XOR of two gates, and any independent tuning of the both-active state, need a grammar in which one constraint can modulate another.

What cardinality two adds over one gate is: two-bit dependence through additive levels (`1, m1, m2, m1*m2`); multi-slot bias under one gate with a shared denominator; gate partitions, where one bit selects which slot or which multiplier is active; switched reading, where the pair mask selects which gate is read; and slot-gate XOR. Each is built from the same two operations, log-weight addition and normalisation.

Higher-order syntax can be dynamically redundant. When complementary conditions assign the same weight, the condition vanishes from the full kernel. When opposite directions on one literal assign the same weight, the slot's own state vanishes. When reciprocal weights sit on flipped literals, two different texts are one kernel. The law determines the affine logit, not the literals that wrote it.

Probability-space coupling is a denominator fact. Different-action gates add their logits independently, and each slot's probability depends on the other's weight only through `m1 + m2 + 4`. That is a normalisation interaction, not a new interaction term in the rule algebra.

Information is a coarse reading of the grammar. It is blind to everything a vertex permutation or a bit complement changes, which includes exactly the placement that 8C showed topology converts into shape. It does not rank effective dimension, reducibility, or structural role. The largest value in the census is one-dimensional, and some three-coordinate laws carry exactly the information of a one-coordinate law.

The local equivalences in D0 are kernel conjugacies. They need no global round to transfer to global dynamics. The global questions that remain are of a different kind: how occupancy and topology weight the distinct, non-equivalent laws.

## W. RS / global-coherence interpretation

Inside this model, a small multiplicative constraint grammar composes additively in event-logit space. Visible dynamics come from normalisation, from occupancy, and from how topology places the reweighted slots. Two higher-order constraints can express a genuinely two-dimensional relational dependence that no single constraint expresses. They cannot express a relation between the two conditions themselves. That is the exact sense in which the cardinality-two grammar is compositional and also bounded.

The collapses are part of the picture. Contextual syntax can be dynamically empty, and different syntax can be one dynamics. A coherence account built on this grammar should therefore attach meaning to the law, the affine logit and its placement, and not to the rule text.

Nothing here shows that a physical or biological system uses this DSL, or that relations in nature compose by adding log weights. Nothing here infers a designer. The analogy to a formal language is an analogy: literal gates, action slots, and log-weight tokens combine by addition into a sentence whose meaning is an event distribution. The grammar is the experimenter's.

The ledger keeps the dimensions apart. The two-gate information is small and exact. Effective gate dimension is an exact structural descriptor. Reducibility is a local-law fact, not a global one. The negative results, no gate-by-gate coefficient, no two-gate XOR, no redundant rule, are boundaries of the grammar, and they are recorded as findings.

```text
a = L10 − L00
b = L01 − L00
d = L11 − L10 − L01 + L00
L(G1, G2) = c + a G1 + b G2 + d G1 G2
```

This is the unique representation. It was verified, with exact rational reconstruction gap 0, on five tables: the conjunction, XOR, XNOR, an additive table and a generic one. The interaction coefficient `d` is exactly the second discrete difference. In these coordinates, the 8D K2-only grammar is the subspace `d = 0`, and one K3 rule supplies `d ≠ 0`.

All four basis features are executable ordinary rules: `A => m`, `A | present(T1) => m`, `A | present(T2) => m` and `A | present(T1) & present(T2) => m`. With continuous positive multipliers, `ln m` is any real number, so these four rules represent every four-corner table.

## Q. Corner-literal basis

A K3 rule selects one raw gate corner. As raw polynomials, in the order (1, G1, G2, G1G2):

```text
[G1=0, G2=0] = 1 − G1 − G2 + G1G2    (1, −1, −1,  1)
[G1=1, G2=0] =      G1      − G1G2   (0,  1,  0, −1)
[G1=0, G2=1] =           G2 − G1G2   (0,  0,  1, −1)
[G1=1, G2=1] =                G1G2   (0,  0,  0,  1)
```

The matrix has determinant 1, so the corner indicators are a second basis of the same four-dimensional space. In it, a table's coefficients are simply its four corner values, and the change of basis to Möbius coefficients is the formula in §P.

**Grammar basis versus finite alphabet.** With at most one W4 rule per basis element (no rule, or one of four grades), each basis reaches 625 distinct four-corner tables:

- In log2 units, the corner basis reaches every table whose corners lie in {0, ±1, ±2}.
- The polynomial basis reaches corners up to ±8 in log2.
- The two sets share 279 tables, and each reaches 346 that the other does not.

Algebraic completeness holds for both bases. Finite-alphabet coverage differs between them, and neither contains the other.

## R. XOR and XNOR constructions

These are targeted constructions on one placement, the action `0-1` with gates `0-1-2` and `0-1-3`, at every W4 grade and in both directions. They are not a K3-pair census.

- `A | G1 & NOT G2 => m` with `A | NOT G1 & G2 => m` gives multiplier 1 at (0,0) and (1,1), and `m` at (0,1) and (1,0): an exact XOR-gated action. In raw Möbius coefficients this is `a = b = ln m`, `d = −2 ln m`.
- `A | G1 & G2 => m` with `A | NOT G1 & NOT G2 => m` gives `m` at the equal corners and 1 at the mixed ones: XNOR. Here `c = ln m`, `a = b = −ln m`, `d = 2 ln m`.

Both match on all 1,024 states with kernel gap 0, and no other gate state receives the multiplier. Generation 8D found that two K2 rules cannot isolate XOR. Two K3 rules do.

Four mutually exclusive K3 corner rules assign four independent multipliers. With `strong_suppress`, `weak_suppress`, `weak_favour` and `strong_favour` on corners 00, 01, 10 and 11, the measured gate table is 1/4, 1/2, 2, 4, exact, because exactly one corner rule matches any gate state. With continuous weights, any four positive multipliers are reachable this way. Under W4 each corner is limited to {1, 1/4, 1/2, 2, 4}.

The Boolean structure is in the gate-selection feature: which gate states apply a multiplier to one action slot. The six-slot event law is still a normalised weight, and the transition function as a whole is not Boolean.

## S. Rule cardinality versus expression complexity

| System | Rule cardinality | Max per-rule K | Effective gate dimension | Gate interaction order | Distinct law rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| two K2 rules, one action, two gates (8D, e.g. ORB-0001-W00) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 3–4 |
| one K3 conjunction (8E, any system) | 1 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| two K3 rules, XOR or XNOR (8E construction) | 2 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| four K3 corner rules (8E construction, W4 grades 1/4, 1/2, 2, 4) | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 5 |

The vector is not summed. Cardinality and K move independently. The last row is worth noticing. The measured four-corner assignment has log2 corner values −2, −1, +1, +2 at 00, 01, 10, 11. That is `−2 + 3 G1 + G2` with `d = 0`, so four K3 rules wrote a law with no gate×gate term at all. Syntactic K bounds the interaction order. It does not fix it, and the coefficients decide. Two K2 rules raise cardinality without raising the interaction order. One K3 rule raises the order at cardinality 1. The two-gate XOR needs both.

## T. What balanced information can and cannot see

Grouping the 80 systems by grade, literal-polarity relation and incidence class gives 24 groups, and each group has one information value. Further, only 4 distinct values occur in the census, one per grade. Action direction, literal polarity, incidence and placement are all invisible to balanced information, exactly as for one gate in 8C and for two gates in 8D. The balanced measure is uniform on the 1,024 states, and complementing a bit or permuting vertices preserves it.

The local law is not placement-blind: the 80 systems are 80 distinct S4 classes. A labelled source graph will also respond differently according to where the action sits (Generation 8C). No trajectory atlas is run here.

## V. Inferences

Within this DSL, expression complexity and rule cardinality are different operations on the event logit. A rule contributes one log weight times the product of its literal truths, so a rule reading r literals adds a term of interaction order r. Adding rules sums such terms. K therefore supplies gate×gate interaction that increasing the cardinality of K2 rules cannot.

The ordinary grammar is already hierarchically complete over two gates when weights are continuous: `K ≤ 3` rules, through either basis, express every four-corner action-logit table, including XOR and the independent tuning of the both-active state that 8D could not reach. What 8D found was the boundary of a subgrammar.

Meta-constraints are therefore not needed for a gate×gate term, or for two-gate XOR. If they add expressivity, it must be something no fixed set of higher-K ordinary rules reproduces: for example, one relation changing another rule's coefficient, existence, polarity or structure. That question stays open.

The finite alphabet is a separate constraint. Basis completeness is algebraic. What W4 can actually execute depends on the basis used, and the two bases cover different tables.

## W. RS / global-coherence interpretation

Inside this model, a small constraint grammar has an ordinary compositional hierarchy. Increasing expression complexity introduces progressively higher-order relational features in the event logit, and rule cardinality composes the features available at each level additively. Visible dynamics still come from normalisation, occupancy and topology.

For the broader account, this keeps three ideas apart that are easily run together: that a higher-order relation exists (O), that one constraint reads several relations jointly (K), and that several constraints coexist (cardinality). A higher-order effect in a description is not, by itself, evidence for any one of them.

None of this shows that nature uses Boolean polynomials, that physical law is a softmax, that higher K is more fundamental, or that a Designer is established. It is a statement about this DSL.

# Generation 8E: scope qualification

External Review 008E qualifies the historical general-r theorem. The Generation
8E report, its published tables and its immutable snapshot remain unchanged.

The intended statement is: a non-neutral ordinary rule whose r condition literals
refer to r distinct gate variables and are jointly satisfiable contributes an
r-way conjunctive feature and has non-zero top interaction order r over those
variables, on an admissible action and over the independently available gates.

For such literals, the action log multiplier is ln(m) times their product. Its
top raw-gate coefficient is ln(m) times the product of the literal signs. This
coefficient is non-zero when m differs from 1.

The parser accepts `present(T) & absent(T)` on the same triad. This conjunction
is unsatisfiable, never matches and contributes a zero local law, not order 2.
Repeating a satisfiable gate variable also does not introduce a new independent
variable. Consequently syntactic condition count alone cannot establish order.

The E0 census already required two distinct triads and non-neutral W4 grades, so
its 80 local interaction results are unaffected. The historical finding
`F8E-GENERAL-K-INTERACTION` retains its wording and is marked `qualified`.
`F8F-GENERAL-K-SCOPE` supplies the qualification through a `qualifies` relation.

Weights and successors use the existing toggle kernel. W4 weights are exact

deterministic high-precision kernel-derived, not mathematically exact irrational

The existing 8B block solve sums triad-only events until the next pair toggle.

1,2,4,8,16,32,64. Marginals retain 64 pair masks, 11 graph classes and seven edge

defines every index. [All checkpoint distributions](tables/generation-008f-checkpoint-distributions.json)
and [information cells](tables/generation-008f-checkpoint-bridge.csv) are published.

Each law has one communicating class. The epoch chain has period 2: every pair
event changes edge-count parity. It has a unique stationary occupancy, but a
fixed-parity start does not converge as a full distribution to that occupancy.
Parity-conditioned stationary marginals and decompositions are included rather
than averaging away this clock property.

occupancy difference, while shape conditional on k does not.

## V. Inferences

Pair topology selects which projection can expose a law difference during
routing. Nonlinear normalization, hidden-state motion and event weighting can
turn a centered local logit interaction into marginal occupancy differences.
Matching a balanced mean does not match those weightings. The stationary
factorisation bounds what unlabelled shape can preserve in a single-action,
independent-bit grammar. These conclusions are scoped to this palette.

A large difference may include unmatched lower-order bias; its magnitude alone
does not diagnose interaction order. The three controls supply different questions,
not one scalar interaction-strength measure.

## W. RS / global-coherence interpretation

The bridge adds a dynamical qualification to local expressivity: a new local
coefficient can become transient shape and persistent labelled/edge occupancy,
while some syntactic placement distinctions are erased by independent-bit
symmetry. This is a model result, not evidence that nature uses these logits,
that higher K is more fundamental, or that the ontology should be expanded.
Incidence needs a dynamical coupling before face membership itself can matter.

8C provides one-gate local laws, 8D additive log-weight composition, 8E genuine conjunction interaction, and 8F its visible dynamical routing. The smallest explanatory core is a finite Boolean state, fixed single-bit events, conjunctive rule features, positive multiplicative factors, normalisation and declared projections.

There is no new experimental round, stochastic trajectory, Monte Carlo atlas, parameter search, K4 census, H/L implementation or N5 extension. No G0 is opened: selected representation minima and counterexamples are algebraically derived; tests verify fixed proof fixtures.

[Grammar](../formal/constraint-grammar.md) defines actions, literals, count predicates, factor names, occurrences and normal form. O3 permits pair/triad actions and any non-action pair/triad condition. Both directions encode the action bit. Contradictory literals can parse but never match. O2 has count predicates; O3 rejects them.

The parser/backend and standard experiment runner are not identical: the runner bounds alphabets and J; the core accepts custom factors and unbounded literal conjunctions.

## G. Additive event-logit grammar

CL-T01/T02 prove multiplication of weights and addition of log weights, independent of rule order in exact arithmetic. Multiplicity is not idempotence. Zero prohibit is outside the positive logarithmic theorem. Normalisation couples probabilities even when features add.

## H. K and interaction order

CL-T06 bounds one-literal additive rules; CL-T07/T08 prove nonzero top degree for distinct, satisfiable, non-neutral literal conjunctions on an admissible action. Literal polarity gives a raw-bit sign.

**New scope boundary:** CL-T14 proves that count>=1 at O2,N3 has K=2 but degree 2 over two remaining bits. The K-1 interaction bound is literal-only. This is an additive qualification, not an edit to the historical 8E statement.

## I. Rule cardinality

CL-T13 proves that adding terms within a fixed feature family stays in its span. J can change strengths and nonlinear visible consequences without making an absent log-weight monomial. It is not interchangeable with K or gate dimension.

CL-T21 gives proven selected [min J,min max-K] representations. AND is [1,3], XOR/XNOR [2,3] under both continuous factors and W4-selected target grades. Constant 8 is continuous [1,1], structurally simple W4 [3,2], or stacked W4 [2,1]. No search was needed.

CL-T09/T10 give the alternating-subset coefficient formula, uniqueness and corner-indicator transformation. Ordinary conjunctions supply these features where the literal parser permits them. The proofs are in [derivations](../formal/derivations.md).

[Equivalences](../formal/equivalences.md) separates canonical syntax, weights, full local law, full kernel, conjugacy, projected process and statistic equality. Pair-conditioned local equality is weaker than full-event equality. Common weight scaling preserves q.

## S. Stationary factorisation

**New formal result:** CL-T18 proves factorisation for the entire autonomous single-action independent-bit family: action rates depend only on their own bit and hidden bits; all other pair/hidden flips are symmetric unit rates. It proves both embedded full-event and pair-arrival occupancy using an auxiliary generator and arrival flux, without introducing a physical time axis.

CL-T19 derives shape-given-edge invariance by orbit double-counting. The 8F numerical ~2.6e-15 factorisation gap remains a separate verification, not the proof.

The tempting broader statement fails if the action reads another pair bit. An explicit symbolic balance counterexample has pair-arrival core (18,24,16,30)/88 and non-uniform second-bit marginal. Thus the independence assumption is essential.

The proof is not inherently N4: N5 alone or XOR alone within this family cannot restore stationary shape discrimination. CL-T17 also separates unique stationarity from period-2 fixed-parity limits.

Full current-state event-weight expressivity is **proved with restrictions** by CL-T12: unbounded positive-factor literal parser/backend, existing O2/O3 single-toggle support, K<=D and J<=D*2^D. It does not apply to arbitrary kernel support or the runner's finite W/J bounds.

## V. H versus L

H targets different histories at identical complete ordinary state. L targets different reachable dynamical constraint states under one common program. Current-state meta syntax can compile into ordinary fixed weights when its controller is a function of x; independent rule state changes the represented state.

The permanent compilation test declares state, clock, event support, projection, priors and budgets before any expressivity claim.

## W. Observations

The implementation audit establishes the parser/core/runner distinctions and count-token boundary. Historical numeric and census outputs are cited, not re-selected. Fixed fixtures verify the formal identities, rational balance construction, state-table constructor, projection decomposition, catalogue schema and preservation of old artifacts.

## X. Inferences

Explanatory compression now removes several weak motivations for expansion: small magnitude does not imply a deficient model; incidence metadata does not imply incidence dynamics; N alone cannot defeat the autonomous single-action stationary theorem.

## Y. RS / global-coherence interpretation

The laboratory supports a scoped model of current relations selecting weighted possibilities through compositional constraints. Higher literal complexity supplies higher log-weight interaction order. This does not establish physical spacetime, ultimate receiver, design, theology or natural implementation of the DSL.

The book integration map marks mature model statements READY/READY_WITH_SCOPE and defers numeric palette magnitudes and ontology expansions. Both books remain untouched.

## Z. Recommended next research branch

Recommend a **same-full-current-state H>0 history witness**, not its execution. Two legal last-event histories ending at identical x (all pairs and triads) should be evaluated under one common historical controller. Distinct future rows cannot be supplied by larger K/J at unchanged x. Coincident futures, a selector already determined by x, or non-identical complete states would falsify the proposed need.
